Apple___Apple_scab.causes: Venturia inaequalis fungus spreads via water splash in wet spring conditions
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-brown scabby lesions on leaves and fruit, dark spots with raised edges
Apple___Apple_scab.treatment: Apply sulfur or copper fungicides during bud break. Remove infected leaves. Prune for air circulation.
Apple___Apple_scab.prevention: Avoid overhead watering. Remove fallen leaves in autumn. Space trees for ventilation.

Apple___Black_rot.causes: Botryosphaeria fungi from cankers on branches, spread by water and insects
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Dark, sunken, circular lesions on leaves with concentric rings. Fruit shows large dark spots.
Apple___Black_rot.treatment: Prune infected branches. Apply fungicides like thiophanate-methyl. Remove mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.prevention: Remove cankers. Maintain tree vigor. Avoid wounding branches.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.causes: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae fungus, requires both apple and juniper hosts
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange spots with red halos on leaves. Fruit shows similar lesions.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.treatment: Apply sulfur or myclobutanil spray from petal fall to mid-summer. Remove cedar hosts nearby.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.prevention: Plant resistant varieties. Remove eastern red cedar within 1.5 miles if possible.

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Dark green, smooth leaves. No spots, discoloration, or abnormalities.
Apple___healthy.treatment: Maintain regular watering and balanced fertilization.
Apple___healthy.prevention: Continue monitoring weekly. Ensure good pest management practices.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Green, firm leaves with normal texture. No wilting or lesions.
Blueberry___healthy.treatment: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5-5.5). Regular watering during fruit set.
Blueberry___healthy.prevention: Monitor for pests. Prune dead canes annually.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Bright green leaves. No curling, spots, or damage visible.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.treatment: Provide consistent watering and full sunlight.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.prevention: Monitor for cherry slug sawfly. Prune into open vase shape.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.causes: Podosphaera clandestina fungus thrives in warm, humid conditions with poor air circulation
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaves, often on undersides. Leaves may curl and become distorted.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Apply sulfur fungicides or potassium bicarbonate every 10-14 days. Remove infected leaves.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Improve canopy airflow through pruning. Avoid overhead watering at night.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.causes: Cercospora zeae-maydis fungus overwinters on crop residue, favored by warm, wet weather
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Rectangular gray spots with dark borders on leaves. Spots coalesce on susceptible varieties.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.treatment: Apply triazole fungicides at R2-R3 growth stages. Rotate crops. Bury residue.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.prevention: Plant resistant hybrids. Remove affected residue. Use 2-3 year crop rotation.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.causes: Puccinia sorghi fungus produces uredospores spread by wind
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Red-brown pustules on leaf surfaces, arranged in strips. Leaves may yellow and die.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.treatment: Spray triazole fungicides when rust becomes visible. Plant resistant varieties.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.prevention: Destroy volunteer corn. Use rust-resistant hybrids. Clean equipment between fields.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Waxy blue-green leaves without pustules or spots. Leaves stand upright.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.treatment: Maintain proper nitrogen levels. Ensure consistent moisture during growth.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for disease. Rotate crops annually.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.causes: Exserohilum turcicum fungus spread by wind and rain splash, survives on residue
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Gray-green oblong lesions with yellow halos on middle leaves. Lesions elongated parallel to veins.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.treatment: Spray azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin at whorl stage and later. Plant resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.prevention: Bury corn residue. Use resistant varieties. Avoid planting susceptible hybrids in infected fields.

Grape___Black_rot.causes: Guignardia bidwellii fungus produces perithecia in mummified fruit, spread by water splash
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Tan or brown lesions with dark border on leaves. Berries turn brown-black, mummify.
Grape___Black_rot.treatment: Remove mummified berries. Spray mancozeb or captan starting at bloom. Prune for air flow.
Grape___Black_rot.prevention: Clean up fallen fruit. Provide good canopy ventilation. Avoid overhead watering.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).causes: Multiple wood decay fungi (Phaeomoniella, Phaeoacremonium) enter through pruning wounds
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Leaves show tiger-stripe pattern of white and red. Wood shows black streaking inside.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).treatment: Remove severely affected canes. Paint pruning wounds with wound dressing. Remove symptomatic vines.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).prevention: Prune in dry conditions. Avoid wounding vines. Remove infected wood immediately.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Green, turgid leaves. Vines climbing vigorously. No spots or discoloration.
Grape___healthy.treatment: Maintain balanced nutrient program. Provide adequate water during veraison.
Grape___healthy.prevention: Monitor weekly for downy and powdery mildew. Scout for insects.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.causes: Isariopsis clavispora fungus favored by high humidity and warm temperatures
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Small brown circular spots with concentric rings on leaf surface. Spots may coalesce.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.treatment: Apply mancozeb or sulfur every 10-14 days starting at pre-bloom. Remove infected leaves.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.prevention: Thin shoots for air circulation. Avoid spreading spores via equipment. Plant resistant varieties.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).causes: Candidatus Liberibacter bacterium spread by Asian citrus psyllid insect vector
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Yellow mottling on leaves in asymmetric pattern. Fruit is small, green, misshapen.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).treatment: No cure. Remove infected trees (this is mandatory in many regions). Control psyllid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).prevention: Scout for psyllids. Use yellow sticky traps. Quarantine infected plants. Control vectors.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas pruni bacterium spreads via water splash and infected pruning tools
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small angular dark brown spots on leaves with yellow halos. Spots on fruit are corky.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper fungicides after bud break. Sanitize pruning tools. Remove infected branches.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Prune in dry conditions. Space trees for air flow. Use disease-free nursery stock.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Soft, fuzzy green fruits. Leaves are smooth, green, without blemishes.
Peach___healthy.treatment: Thin fruit to 6-8 inches apart for better size. Regular watering during fruit development.
Peach___healthy.prevention: Prune to open vase in winter. Scout for brown rot and leaf curl.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas campestris spread via water splash, tools, and contaminated seeds
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Dark brown spots with yellow halo on leaves. Fruit develops raised lesions.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper oxychloride spray. Remove infected plants. Sanitize stakes and cages.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seeds. Stake to keep canopy off soil. Avoid overhead watering.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Glossy, dark green leaves. Peppers developing with normal color and texture.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.treatment: Provide consistent moisture (1 inch per week). Support with cages.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.prevention: Mulch to retain moisture. Scout for thrips and spider mites.

Potato___Early_blight.causes: Alternaria solani fungus overwinters on infected debris, spread by water and spores
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown lesions with concentric rings (target-like) on lower leaves first. Lesions coalesce.
Potato___Early_blight.treatment: Prune lower leaves at hilling. Spray mancozeb starting at plant closure. Remove infected plants.
Potato___Early_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Avoid overhead watering. Destroy cull piles. Rotate crops 2-3 years.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous green foliage. Leaves are uniform green, no spots or yellowing.
Potato___healthy.treatment: Hill soil around stems. Provide 1-2 inches water weekly.
Potato___healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for late blight and insects. Monitor weather for disease risk.

Potato___Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans oomycete spreads in cool, wet conditions. Can cause tuber rot in soil.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions with white mold on undersides during wet weather. Browns quickly.
Potato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove infected plant tops. Spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days starting at closure.
Potato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Destroy volunteer potatoes. Hill soil over tubers. Improve air flow.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Bright green compound leaves. Canes are upright and vigorous.
Raspberry___healthy.treatment: Remove dead/diseased canes. Thin to 5-6 canes per hill.
Raspberry___healthy.prevention: Remove old fruiting canes after harvest. Scout for anthracnose and rust.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Lush compound leaves on vigorous plants. No spots, wilting, or discoloration.
Soybean___healthy.treatment: Monitor soil moisture before pod fill. Avoid compaction.
Soybean___healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for stem flies and spider mites. Monitor for frogeye leaf spot.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.causes: Podosphaera xanthii fungus thrives in warm, dry conditions with poor air movement
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White powdery coating on leaf surfaces, starting on undersides. Leaves yellow and shrivel.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.treatment: Spray sulfur or potassium bicarbonate weekly starting at first sign. Remove affected leaves.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.prevention: Space plants wider for air flow. Mulch to conserve moisture. Avoid overhead watering.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Bright green leaves with typical three leaflets. Runners visible.
Strawberry___healthy.treatment: Control runners or allow succession plantings. Provide balanced nutrition.
Strawberry___healthy.prevention: Scout weekly for Spider mites and gray mold. Thin for fruit size.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.causes: Diplocarpon earlianum fungus overwinters in dead leaf tissue on plant and debris
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Reddish-purple spots on leaf margins that turn dark brown. Centers become tan.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.treatment: Remove infected leaves and runners. Apply captan or chlorothalonil. Clean up debris.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.prevention: Plant in raised beds with good drainage. Use disease-free plants. Avoid overhead watering.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.causes: Xanthomonas campestris pv. vesicatoria spread via water splash, tools, and hands
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark lesions with yellow halo on leaves and fruit. Lesions are angular.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.treatment: Apply copper hydroxide spray. Remove lower leaves. Sanitize tools between plants.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.prevention: Use disease-free seeds. Space for air flow. Avoid overhead watering. Stake plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.causes: Alternaria solani fungus spreads from lower infected leaves upward in warm, wet conditions
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (target-like) on lower leaves. Spots coalesce.
Tomato___Early_blight.treatment: Remove infected leaves. Spray mancozeb starting when spots appear. Bottom leaves first.
Tomato___Early_blight.prevention: Prune lower leaves (6 inches). Mulch to avoid soil splash. Use resistant varieties.

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Dark green leaves with no spots or lesions. Plants are vigorous and erect.
Tomato___healthy.treatment: Maintain consistent watering (1.5 inches per week). Suckers optional.
Tomato___healthy.prevention: Scout daily for early/late blight and insects. Maintain good canopy.
Tomato___healthy.chatbot_context: Tomato is a high-value crop. Ask about specific symptoms, fruit quality, or irrigation.

Tomato___Late_blight.causes: Phytophthora infestans oomycete spreads in cool (60-70F), wet weather. Can cause fruit rot.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked gray-green lesions with white mold on undersides. Lesions brown quickly.
Tomato___Late_blight.treatment: Remove affected plant parts immediately. Spray chlorothalonil or mancozeb every 7-10 days.
Tomato___Late_blight.prevention: Use resistant varieties. Space for air flow. Mulch soil. Remove infected debris immediately.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.causes: Cladosporium fulvum fungus thrives in high humidity (>85%) and warm temps (65-75F)
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale yellow spots on leaf tops, olive-gray mold on undersides. Leaves yellow and drop.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.treatment: Improve ventilation. Reduce humidity. Spray chlorothalonil or sulfur. Remove infected leaves.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.prevention: Increase spacing. Morning watering only. Bottom-side pruning. Use resistant varieties.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.causes: Septoria lycopersici fungus overwinters on debris, spread by water splash and tools
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Circular spots with dark borders and gray centers with minute black dots (pycnidia).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.treatment: Remove lower infected leaves. Spray mancozeb or chlorothalonil every 10-14 days.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.prevention: Mulch to prevent splash. Remove debris. Prune lower leaves. Use drip irrigation.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.causes: Two-spotted spider mites (Tetranychus urticae) thrive in hot, dry conditions
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine webbing on leaves and stems. Yellow stippling on leaves that turn brown.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.treatment: Spray strong water spray or neem oil. Apply sulfur. Spray insecticidal soap.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.prevention: Increase humidity. Keep weeds down. Remove infested leaves. Monitor weekly.

Tomato___Target_Spot.causes: Corynespora cassiicola fungus spread via water splash in warm, humid conditions
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Small circular lesions with concentric rings (target-like). Yellow halo around spots.
Tomato___Target_Spot.treatment: Remove infected leaves. Spray mancozeb or copper fungicides every 7-10 days.
Tomato___Target_Spot.prevention: Improve air circulation. Avoid overhead watering. Remove debris. Use resistant varieties.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.causes: Virus spread by hands, tools, and insect vectors (not seed). Persists on surfaces.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Leaves show mosaic pattern (mottled green/yellow). Growth stunted. Fruit misshapen.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.treatment: No cure. Remove infected plants. Sanitize ALL tools, stakes, and hands with 10% bleach.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.prevention: Wash hands before touching plants. Disinfect tools. Remove weeds (some hosts). No smoking.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.causes: Virus spread by whitefly vector (Bemisia tabaci). Cannot be spread by hands or tools.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Lower leaves curl and yellow. Plant is severely stunted. No fruit production.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.treatment: Remove infected plants immediately. Control whiteflies with insecticidal soap or neem.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.prevention: Scout for whiteflies weekly. Use yellow sticky traps. Remove infected plants early.
